milestone: 2a: a generated district where the street wall and the lots fit

tasks.goal: Fill in rowDepth and rowRuns in src/sim/layout.js so every street-wall row on a generated district stays off the crossings and never backs into the row facing it.
tasks.commit: feat(layout): street-wall rows derived from the roads
tasks.notes: The comments above each function in layout.js are the exact rules; the constants are final, do not change them. Use only the district passed in, never world.js globals. Avenues are not sorted by x in every district.

tasks.goal: Fill in deriveLots and planLayout in src/sim/layout.js so every generated district gets 6 to 12 lots set into its rows, and the plan cuts those lots and the pinned towers out of the rows.
tasks.commit: feat(layout): zonable lots derived from the rows and the seed
tasks.notes: Seed the randomness with mulberry32 from src/sim/rng.js, never Math.random. Keep each lot's avenue and side while you place it (an internal helper can return them); deriveLots returns only [x, z, w, d]. rowDepth and rowRuns are done and tested; build on them.

tasks.goal: Make createCity in src/sim/zoning.js zone WORLD_PLAN.lots on a generated world, and keep the hand LOTS table on the hand preset.
tasks.commit: feat(zoning): a generated city zones the lots its layout plan derives
tasks.notes: WORLD_PLAN is exported by src/sim/layout.js and is null on the hand preset. This is a two-line change: import it, and pick WORLD_PLAN.lots or LOTS. Do not touch LOTS itself.

tasks.goal: Make the street wall in src/render/block.js and the frontage meter in scripts/check_overlap.mjs read WORLD_PLAN.rows on a generated world, so row buildings stop overlapping each other, the lots and the roads.
tasks.commit: feat(block): the street wall stands where the layout plan says
tasks.notes: Import WORLD_PLAN from src/sim/layout.js (in check_overlap.mjs, import it after the seed is set, like the other src/ imports there). In streetWall(ax, side, rand): when WORLD_PLAN has a row for this ax and side, use its runs instead of ROW_RUNS minus KEEP_OUT, and cap each building's w at the row's depth. Keep calling rand() the same number of times. In the checker's frontage loop, use the same plan runs when there is a plan. With no plan (the hand preset) nothing may change: npm run check:overlap must print the same numbers as before.
